---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner of the Grok Bot backup template; asks for
  the default and per-bot Drive destinations, workspace folder routing,
  health-filter opt-out, quiet hours, retention and run times, and checks the
  cookie seed file. Use when backup settings are missing from memory.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: "I back up your Grok Bot setup to your Google Drive every night (bots, settings, skills, routines, memories, transcripts and unsaved code) and your /workspace files every week, with no passwords or keys."

Ask these one at a time, wait for each answer, and offer the default.

1. **Default destination:** "Which Google Drive account and folder should your backups go to?" If that account isn't connected, help them connect it (add-connector skill). Confirm you can reach the folder by listing it with that connector. Record the folder id and the exact connection id (for example `user-Google-drive--work`). This is the default destination: `UNLISTED_AGENTS=include`.
2. **Per-bot routing:** "Should any bots go to a different Drive, for example personal bots to a personal Drive?" Default: no, so every bot goes to the default destination. If yes, repeat question 1 for each extra destination, give each a `LABEL` (for example `work`, `personal`), and set `UNLISTED_AGENTS=exclude` on every destination except the default. Then ask which bots go where, and record `INCLUDE_AGENT_IDS` and `EXCLUDE_AGENT_IDS` by bot id. Work and company data must never go through a personal Drive connector, so a work bot never goes to a personal destination.
3. **Shared items:** "Should your global settings, your own skills, background transcripts and box extras (unsaved code, installed tools, config files and the names of keys you'd need) go with your main backup?" Default: yes, on the work or default destination only (`INCLUDE_SHARED=yes` there and `no` everywhere else).
4. **Workspace folders:** write the script files from the grok-bot-backup skill into `$BACKUP_DIR` first, then run `workspace-backup.sh --dry-run` and show the folder table with sizes. Ask: "Which of these are work and which are personal?" Suggest personal for anything about health, tax, estate, wills, trusts or family legal matters, and work for everything else. Allow `skip` too. Save the answers to `$BACKUP_DIR/workspace-routes.tsv`, one `<folder> work|personal|skip` per line, plus `(top-level files) <route>`. Explain that new folders default to work, and that anything that looks personal is held back until they route it. If everything is personal or work, one destination is enough.
5. **Health memories:** "Is there a health bot whose health memories you want kept in its backup?" Default: no. This is only allowed for a bot whose backup goes to a personal Drive. Record its id in `HEALTH_FILTER_OFF` for that destination. HR, pay and performance memories are always removed.
6. **Quiet hours:** "When should I never message you?" Default: `21:00-07:00` in their time zone. Then ask "Weekends too?" and record `QUIET_HOURS`, `QUIET_DAYS` and `BACKUP_TZ`.
7. **Retention:** "How long should I keep backups?" Defaults: nightly folders 30 days, weekly workspace folders 4 weeks (28 days).
8. **Run times:** default nightly at 2 AM, weekly workspace on Sunday at 3 AM, monthly restore test on the 1st at 4 AM, all in their time zone.

Then:
- **Cookie seed check:** run `find /home/box -maxdepth 4 -name chrome-cookie-seed.json -exec stat -c '%a %n' {} \;`. Never open the file. If the mode lets anyone else read it (any digit after the first one is not 0), tell the owner and, with their OK, run `chmod 600` on it.
- **Memories:** save one memory per destination with `LABEL`, `DRIVE_CONNECTOR`, `DEST_FOLDER_ID` and the folder name, `INCLUDE_AGENT_IDS`, `EXCLUDE_AGENT_IDS`, `UNLISTED_AGENTS`, `INCLUDE_SHARED`, `HEALTH_FILTER_OFF` and `WS_ROUTE`. Save one global memory with `BACKUP_DIR=/workspace/grokbot-backup`, `BACKUP_TZ`, `QUIET_HOURS`, `QUIET_DAYS`, `NIGHTLY_RETENTION_DAYS`, `WORKSPACE_RETENTION_DAYS` and the run times. Never save a key, token or password.
- **Scripts:** make sure every script file from the grok-bot-backup skill is in `$BACKUP_DIR`.
- **Routines:** create the nightly, weekly workspace and monthly restore-test routines with the template's prompts. If quiet hours are set, also offer the morning-notices routine at the end of quiet hours.
- **Mac roster:** offer the Mac roster script from the grok-bot-backup skill. Explain in two sentences that it captures sidebar sections, pinned bots, voices and local permission settings, and that they upload the result to the backup folder itself.
- **Usage questions:** if they ask what the backup costs in tokens or credits, say you can't see your own usage and point them to the Usage page in Grok Bot settings. Never guess a number.
- **Test run:** with their OK, run the nightly backup once for each destination and the workspace backup once. Then share the Drive links, any chats that had tokens redacted (so live keys can be replaced), any held-back folders and anything missing.

# Grok Bot Backup

Goal: anyone can rebuild this whole Grok Bot setup from Drive after losing the computer, and no password, key or token is ever stored. This skill is self-contained. A fresh owner needs nothing else: the scripts are at the end, and getting-started collects the settings.

Never copy or upload passwords, tokens, cookies, login files, keychain items, .ssh, .env files, credential caches, the box's own secret files or browser profiles. Every script here is read-only on the data it backs up. None of them commits, pushes, stashes or changes a git repo.

## 0. Setup and inputs

Read the settings from memory. If any are missing, stop and run getting-started.

Per destination (one set per Drive, for example `work` and `personal`):
- `LABEL`: the run's name. It appears in archive names.
- `DEST_FOLDER_ID` and `DRIVE_CONNECTOR`: the Drive folder and the exact connection id that owns it. Always upload a destination's files through its own connector. Work and company data must never land in a personal Drive.
- `INCLUDE_AGENT_IDS` and `EXCLUDE_AGENT_IDS`: comma lists of bot ids (names also work).
- `UNLISTED_AGENTS`: `include` for the owner's default destination and `exclude` for every other one, so a new bot lands in exactly one place.
- `INCLUDE_SHARED`: `yes` or `no`. It controls whether global settings, user skills, agent transcripts and the box-extras archive go along. Use `yes` for exactly one destination, normally work.
- `HEALTH_FILTER_OFF`: bots whose health memories are kept. Only allow this on a destination that goes to a personal Drive. HR, pay and performance lines are always removed.
- `WS_ROUTE`: which workspace route this destination takes (`work` or `personal`).

Global settings: `BACKUP_DIR` (default `/workspace/grokbot-backup`; it must be under /workspace so uploads work), `BACKUP_TZ`, `QUIET_HOURS` (for example `21:00-07:00`), `QUIET_DAYS` (for example `Sat,Sun`), `NIGHTLY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30), `WORKSPACE_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 28) and the route file `$BACKUP_DIR/workspace-routes.tsv`. Each line of the route file is `<top-level folder> work|personal|skip`. Use `(top-level files)` for loose files.

Scripts: if any file listed in "Scripts" below is missing from `$BACKUP_DIR` or differs from its block, copy the old one to `<name>.bak-YYYY-MM-DD`, write the block exactly, and `chmod +x` the `.sh` files. All five files must sit together in `$BACKUP_DIR`.

## Nightly backup (repeat for each destination)

1. **Stage.** Use that destination's Drive connector to find the newest `grokbot-roster-*.md` in `DEST_FOLDER_ID` itself, not in a dated subfolder. Download it with DownloadFile into `$BACKUP_DIR/device-roster/`. Then write these into `$BACKUP_DIR/inputs/$LABEL/`, covering included bots only:
   - `connectors.md`: name, type and status of each connector, with no secrets.
   - `bot-exports.md`: one `## <bot name>` section per bot, holding its routine prompts, sidebar section and a `### Memories` bullet list, or "not available".
   - `transcripts-YYYY-MM-DD.md`: one `## <chat name>` section per chat, from the transcript tool. If you have no transcript tool, skip this file and the script uses each bot's store.db instead.
   Inputs live outside the output folder, so a rerun never loses them.
2. **Memory filter.** The script drops HR, pay, performance and health lines from every `### Memories` list. For bots in `HEALTH_FILTER_OFF`, it keeps the health lines.
3. **Secret scan and redact.** The script redacts transcripts, config files, settings and code patches, replacing each hit with `[REDACTED:type]` and then scanning again. A file that still has a hit, or a binary file with a hit, is left out and listed in the README. The run itself does not fail. `sk-` keys match only at a word boundary, and password fields inside escaped JSON are caught.
4. **Manifest and archive.** Run `$BACKUP_DIR/run-backup.sh` with the step 0 settings as environment variables. If `INCLUDE_SHARED=yes`, also run `$BACKUP_DIR/box-extras.sh` with the same `LABEL` and `WORKSPACE_ROUTES`. Outputs go to `$BACKUP_DIR/out/<label>-YYYY-MM-DD/`, together with `upload-list.tsv` (file name and byte size). If a script stops because an archive exists, rerun it with `ARCHIVE_NAME=grok-bot-backup-<label>-YYYY-MM-DD-v2.tar.gz` (or `EXTRAS_ARCHIVE_NAME=...`). Never delete a backup to make room. If a script exits non-zero for any other reason, stop that destination and report it.
5. **Upload.** In `DEST_FOLDER_ID`, find or create a folder named `YYYY-MM-DD` (create_folder on that connector). Upload every file in `upload-list.tsv` with UploadFile, using `connection` = `DRIVE_CONNECTOR`, `destination.folderId` = the dated folder, and `convertToGoogleFormat` left off. Drive keeps duplicate names, so add `-v2` to a name rather than replacing a file.
6. **Verify.** For each upload, call get_file_metadata on the returned id and compare its `size` to `upload-list.tsv`. Folder listings and search lag right after an upload, so never use them to verify. Retry a mismatch once. If it still differs, report it.
7. **Retention.** List `DEST_FOLDER_ID` and trash (trash_file) only folders whose name is exactly a date `YYYY-MM-DD` older than `NIGHTLY_RETENTION_DAYS`. Never touch `workspace-*` folders, roster files or anything else. The scripts prune old local copies under `$BACKUP_DIR/out/` on their own.
8. **Cleanup.** Delete `$BACKUP_DIR/inputs/$LABEL/` and `$BACKUP_DIR/staging/`. Keep `device-roster/`, `out/`, the scripts and the route file.
9. **Report.** Follow "Messaging the owner" below.

## Weekly workspace backup (keep 4 weeks)

/workspace can hold several GB of work, so it is backed up weekly instead of nightly. For each destination:
1. If the route file is missing, run `workspace-backup.sh --dry-run`, show the owner the folder table and ask them to route each folder. Until they answer, back up only the folders that are clearly work.
2. Run `LABEL=<label> WS_ROUTE=<work|personal> BACKUP_DIR=... $BACKUP_DIR/workspace-backup.sh`. It uses an exclude list: node_modules, virtual environments, .git, caches, browser data, credential files, files over 100 MB, the backup folder itself and `agent-tools`. Files that contain a secret pattern are left out and listed. Folders routed elsewhere are skipped. New folders default to `WS_DEFAULT_ROUTE` (work), but anything that looks personal (health, medical, tax, estate, wills, trust, family, legal, kids, bank) is held back and listed in `HELD-BACK-<label>.txt` until the owner routes it. An archive over 500 MB is split into `.part-000`, `.part-001` and so on.
3. Create `workspace-YYYY-MM-DD` in `DEST_FOLDER_ID`, upload every file in `upload-list.tsv`, and verify each by its metadata size as in nightly step 6.
4. Trash only `workspace-YYYY-MM-DD` folders older than `WORKSPACE_RETENTION_DAYS` (28). Never touch a dated nightly folder.
5. Delete the local `out/workspace-*` copy after a verified upload. Report held-back folders or secret-pattern files, quietly, as described below.

## Monthly restore test

A backup nobody has tested can't be trusted. Once a month, for each destination:
1. In Drive, find the newest dated nightly folder and the newest `workspace-*` folder. Download their `.tar.gz` and `.part-*` files with DownloadFile into `$BACKUP_DIR/restore-test/in/` (DownloadFile only writes under /workspace).
2. Run `$BACKUP_DIR/restore-test.sh $BACKUP_DIR/restore-test/in $BACKUP_DIR/restore-test/report-YYYY-MM-DD.md`. It rejoins parts, unpacks each archive in a scratch folder, checks every file's size and sha256 against its MANIFEST.tsv, checks that git bundles can be read, rescans for secrets, and then deletes the scratch copy.
3. Delete `restore-test/in/`. Keep the report. Tell the owner only on FAIL, or during the first month as a one-line "restore test passed". The restore test never prunes anything.

## Messaging the owner

- Stay silent when everything works.
- Message only on: a failed run, a size mismatch after retry, a file left out because it couldn't be redacted, `REDACTED in chat` lines, `NEW BOTS` lines (ask which destination), held-back workspace folders, a readable cookie seed, a disconnected connector, or a device roster missing for several nights.
- For redacted tokens, name each chat or file so the owner can replace any key that is still live. Never quote the token.
- Quiet hours: outside `QUIET_HOURS` and `QUIET_DAYS`, send right away. Inside them, append the note to `$BACKUP_DIR/pending-notices.md` and save a short memory. Deliver held notes with the first message outside quiet hours (the optional morning-notices routine does this), then clear the file. Only send during quiet hours if a secret may already be in Drive (a verify step found one), which needs fast action.
- Token usage: you can't see your own token or credit usage. If asked, say so plainly and point the owner to the Usage page in Grok Bot settings. Never estimate a number.

## Device roster from the owner's computer

Sidebar sections, pinned bots, voices and local permission settings live only in the desktop app. Offer the owner the Mac script below. They run it in Terminal with `bash extract-grokbot-roster.sh` (add `--debug` to print blob names and key names, never values; it needs Python 3). They check the resulting `grokbot-roster-YYYY-MM-DD.md` and upload it to the backup folder itself, not a dated subfolder. The script only reads files, skips cookie, login, token, secret and keychain files, and redacts secret-looking values. Auto-review settings live in the Grok Bot account, not on the device.

## Restoring

Create the bots from `roster.md` and `agent/<id>/profile.json`. Reconnect connectors from `connectors.md` and sign in again; `required-keys-list-<label>.md` lists each key name and re-login the box needs. Copy `shared/workflows/` back as user skills. Recreate routines from `bot-exports.md`. Reinstall software from `box-extras/install/`. For each repo, clone its remote from `remotes.tsv`, fetch `unpushed.bundle`, apply `uncommitted.patch` and copy `untracked/` back. Unpack the workspace parts with `cat <name>.part-* > <name>` and then `tar -xzf`.

## Known limits

- The box can't read routines or memories of other bots stored on the server. Export them through the bot's own tools into `bot-exports.md`, or mark them "not available".
- Built-in platform skills are listed by name only (some contain public API keys that would trip the secret scan) and come back with the platform.
- Secrets are never backed up, so a restore always means signing in again.

## Scripts

Write each block to `$BACKUP_DIR/<file name>` exactly as shown.

### gbb_lib.py
Shared helpers: secret patterns, redaction, manifests, memory filter, workspace routing.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Grok Bot Backup v4 shared helpers: secret patterns, redaction, manifests, memory filter.
# Never prints a secret value: reports give file, pattern type and count only.
import os,re,sys,json,hashlib
P=[('private-key',r'-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----[\s\S]*?(?:-----END [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|$)'),
 ('bearer',r'(?i)\bbearer\s+([\w.~+/=-]{16,})'),
 ('basic-auth',r'(?i)\bauthorization\\*"?\s*[:=]\s*\\*"?basic\s+([\w+/=]{12,})'),
 ('jwt',r'\beyJ[\w-]{8,}\.[\w-]{8,}\.[\w-]{8,}'),
 ('api-key',r'\b(?:sk|pk|rk)-(?:[a-z]+-)?[\w-]{16,}'),
 ('xai-key',r'\bxai-[\w-]{20,}'),
 ('github',r'\b(?:gh[pousr]_\w{20,}|github_pat_\w{20,})'),
 ('slack',r'\bxox[abprs]-[\w-]{10,}'),
 ('aws',r'\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b'),
 ('google-key',r'\bAIza[\w-]{30,}'),
 ('google-oauth',r'\bya29\.[\w-]{20,}'),
 ('url-credentials',r'\b[a-z][\w+.-]*://[^/\s:@"\']+:([^@\s/"\']{3,})@'),
 ('password',r'(?i)\\*"[\w-]*(?:password|passwd|pwd|passphrase)[\w-]*\\*"\s*:\s*\\*"((?!\[RED)[^"\\]{3,})'),
 ('secret-field',r'(?i)\b(?:api[_-]?key|secret|access[_-]?token|refresh[_-]?token|auth[_-]?token|client[_-]?secret|password|passwd)\b\\*"?\s*[:=]\s*\\*"?((?!\[RED)(?!\$\{?[A-Z_])(?!os\.environ)(?!process\.env)[\w./+=-]{8,})')]
P=[(n,re.compile(r)) for n,r in P]
SENS_KEY=re.compile(r'(?i)key|secret|token|password|cookie|credential')
SECRET_NAME=re.compile(r'(?i)(^|/)(\.env(\..*)?|\.netrc|\.git-credentials|\.pgpass|id_(rsa|dsa|ecdsa|ed25519)(\.pub)?|known_hosts|hosts\.yml|credentials?(\.json)?|.*cookie.*|login data.*|.*secret.*|.*token.*\.json|.*\.(pem|key|p12|pfx|kdbx|keychain)|gateway\.json|chrome-cookie-seed\.json)$')
def redact(s,h):
    for n,r in P:
        def f(m,n=n):
            h[n]=h.get(n,0)+1; t=f'[REDACTED:{n}]'
            return m.group(0)[:m.start(1)-m.start()]+t+m.group(0)[m.end(1)-m.start():] if r.groups else t
        s=r.sub(f,s)
    return s
def scan(s): return sorted({n for n,r in P if r.search(s)})
def red_json(o):
    if isinstance(o,dict): return {k:('[redacted]' if SENS_KEY.search(k) and v not in('',None) and not isinstance(v,(dict,list,bool)) else red_json(v)) for k,v in o.items()}
    if isinstance(o,list): return [red_json(v) for v in o]
    if isinstance(o,str) and o[:1] in '{[':
        try: return json.dumps(red_json(json.loads(o)))
        except Exception: pass
    return o
def sha(p):
    h=hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p,'rb') as f:
        for b in iter(lambda:f.read(1<<20),b''): h.update(b)
    return h.hexdigest()
def redact_tree(root,report,skip=()):
    """Redact every text file in place, rescan, drop files that still hit or binary files that hit.
    report: dict with 'redacted' {file:{type:n}} and 'dropped' [(file,reason)]."""
    for d,_,fs in os.walk(root):
        for f in fs:
            p=os.path.join(d,f); rel=os.path.relpath(p,root)
            if rel in skip or os.path.islink(p): continue
            if SECRET_NAME.search(rel): os.remove(p); report['dropped'].append((rel,'secret-looking file name')); continue
            raw=open(p,'rb').read()
            try: s=raw.decode('utf-8'); text=b'\x00' not in raw
            except UnicodeDecodeError: s=raw.decode('latin-1'); text=False
            if not scan(s): continue
            if not text: os.remove(p); report['dropped'].append((rel,'binary file with secret pattern: '+','.join(scan(s)))); continue
            h={}; s2=redact(s,h); left=scan(s2)
            if left: os.remove(p); report['dropped'].append((rel,'could not redact cleanly: '+','.join(left))); continue
            open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s2); report['redacted'][rel]=h
def write_manifest(root,out,extra_note=''):
    rows=[]
    for d,_,fs in os.walk(root):
        for f in fs:
            p=os.path.join(d,f); rel=os.path.relpath(p,root)
            if rel=='MANIFEST.tsv' or os.path.islink(p): continue
            rows.append((rel,os.path.getsize(p),sha(p)))
    with open(out,'w') as o:
        o.write('# path\tsize\tsha256\n')
        for r in sorted(rows): o.write('%s\t%d\t%s\n'%r)
    return rows
MEM={'hr':r'\b(HR|PIP)\b|(?i:\b(human resources|hiring|fired|terminat\w+|disciplin\w+|grievance|layoffs?)\b)',
 'pay':r'(?i)\b(salar\w+|pay ?rate|payroll|compensation|bonus\w*|raises?|wages?|stock options)\b',
 'performance':r'(?i)\b(performance (review|rating|plan|improvement)|perf review|underperform\w*)\b',
 'health':r'(?i)\b(health|medical|diagnos\w+|medication|prescri\w+|therap\w+|doctor|symptoms?|illness|pregnan\w+|disabilit\w+|surgery)\b'}
MEM={k:re.compile(v) for k,v in MEM.items()}
def memory_filter(path,health_off_names):
    """Drop HR, pay, performance and health bullets under any '# ...memor...' heading of a '## <bot>' section.
    Bots whose heading contains a name in health_off_names keep health lines (HR, pay, performance still dropped)."""
    dropped={}; o=[]; bot=''; mem=False
    for ln in open(path,encoding='utf-8'):
        m=re.match(r'(#+)\s*(.*)',ln)
        if m: bot=m[2].lower() if len(m[1])<=2 else bot; mem='memor' in m[2].lower()
        elif mem and ln.lstrip()[:1] in '-*':
            ks=[k for k,r in MEM.items() if r.search(ln) and not (k=='health' and any(x and x in bot for x in health_off_names))]
            for k in ks: dropped[k]=dropped.get(k,0)+1
            if ks: continue
        o.append(ln)
    open(path,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(''.join(o)); return dropped
PERSONAL=re.compile(r'(?i)(?<![a-z])(health|medic|doctor|therap|dental|insur|tax|irs\b|1040|w-?2\b|estate|trust|wills?\b|probate|famil|divorce|custody|kids|child|personal|private|bank|mortgage|legal|lawyer|attorney|journal|diary)')
def load_routes(path):
    r={}
    if path and os.path.exists(path):
        for ln in open(path):
            ln=ln.split('#',1)[0].strip()
            if not ln: continue
            k,_,v=ln.replace('\t',' ').rpartition(' '); r[k.strip().strip('/')]=v.strip().lower()
    return r
def route(name,routes,default='work'):
    """Return (route, why). Unlisted personal-looking names are held back."""
    if name in routes: return routes[name],'listed'
    if PERSONAL.search(name): return 'hold','new folder that looks personal'
    return default,'new folder, default'
if __name__=='__main__':
    cmd=sys.argv[1]
    if cmd=='scan-file':  # exit 1 if a file has secret patterns; prints types only
        s=open(sys.argv[2],'rb').read().decode('utf-8','replace'); t=scan(s); print(','.join(t)); sys.exit(1 if t else 0)
    if cmd=='redact-tree':
        rep={'redacted':{},'dropped':[]}; redact_tree(sys.argv[2],rep); json.dump(rep,open(sys.argv[3],'w'),indent=1)
    if cmd=='manifest': write_manifest(sys.argv[2],sys.argv[3])
```

### run-backup.sh
Nightly bot backup for one destination.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Grok Bot Backup v4: nightly bot backup for one destination. Read-only on source data.
# Usage: LABEL=work BACKUP_DIR=/workspace/grokbot-backup [step 0 env vars] ./run-backup.sh [YYYY-MM-DD]
# Inputs (env): LABEL, BACKUP_DIR, BACKUP_TZ, INCLUDE_AGENT_IDS, EXCLUDE_AGENT_IDS, UNLISTED_AGENTS (include|exclude),
#   INCLUDE_SHARED (yes|no), HEALTH_FILTER_OFF (bot ids or names), RETENTION_DAYS (local copies), ARCHIVE_NAME,
#   DEST_FOLDER_ID and DRIVE_CONNECTOR (recorded in the README only; the agent uploads).
# Output: $BACKUP_DIR/out/<label>-<date>/ with the archive, README.md, roster.md, MANIFEST.tsv, upload-list.tsv.
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"; LIB="$HERE/gbb_lib.py"; [ -f "$LIB" ] || { echo "missing $LIB" >&2; exit 1; }
DATE="${1:-$(date +%F)}"; L="${LABEL:-${OWNER_LABEL:?set LABEL}}"; ROOT="${BACKUP_DIR:?set BACKUP_DIR}"
S="${AGENT_DATA:-/home/box/agent-data}"; HB="${BOX_HOME:-/home/box}"; IN="$ROOT/inputs/$L"; OUT="$ROOT/out/$L-$DATE"; T="$ROOT/staging/$L"
yn(){ case "${1,,}" in y|yes|1|true) echo 1;; *) echo 0;; esac; }
export DATE LABEL="$L" BACKUP_TZ="${BACKUP_TZ:-UTC}" INCLUDE_AGENT_IDS="${INCLUDE_AGENT_IDS:-${INCLUDE_BOTS:-}}" EXCLUDE_AGENT_IDS="${EXCLUDE_AGENT_IDS:-${EXCLUDE_BOTS:-}}"
export UNLISTED_AGENTS="${UNLISTED_AGENTS:-${NEW_BOTS:-include}}" HEALTH_FILTER_OFF="${HEALTH_FILTER_OFF:-${KEEP_HEALTH_BOTS:-}}" SHARED="$(yn "${INCLUDE_SHARED:-${SHARED:-yes}}")"
```

routines.name: Nightly Grok Bot backup
routines.description: Fires every night to back up all bots, settings, skills, memories, transcripts and box extras to Google Drive and prune old dated folders.
routines.content:
Run tonight's Grok Bot backup with the grok-bot-backup skill (nightly section, steps 0 to 9). Inputs: the backup settings saved in memory, one set per destination (LABEL, DRIVE_CONNECTOR, DEST_FOLDER_ID, INCLUDE_AGENT_IDS, EXCLUDE_AGENT_IDS, UNLISTED_AGENTS, INCLUDE_SHARED, HEALTH_FILTER_OFF, WS_ROUTE), plus BACKUP_DIR, BACKUP_TZ, quiet hours and NIGHTLY_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30). If there are no settings, stop and tell the owner to finish setup with getting-started. Run each destination in turn through its own Drive connector only. Upload to a dated YYYY-MM-DD folder, verify each file by its metadata size, and trash only dated folders older than the retention period. Never copy passwords, tokens, cookies, login files or browser profiles. Stay silent when everything works, and follow the skill's quiet-hours rules for anything else.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 2 * * *`
